objective: Make the selected X1 mechanical/electrical packaging tolerant of trail dust, grit, mud and splash while preserving drainage, inspection and service recovery.

standards_references.role: reference structure for protection of road-vehicle electrical enclosures against foreign objects/dust and water
reference for controlled comparative corrosion exposure of material/coating specimens
standards_references.caveat: ASTM states stand-alone salt-spray results do not reliably predict natural-environment performance

environmental_layers.purpose: identify every enclosure seam, connector, vent/drain, bearing, brake and harness entry that can trap or admit contamination
expose binding, seal, drain, fastener and service vulnerabilities without water or high energy
verify intended splash paths, drainage and dry protected zones using an inert enclosure
verify that viscous contamination does not block drainage, service access, steering/brake motion or cooling paths
prove disconnected interfaces can be inspected, cleaned and fully re-seated without seal or pin damage
detect retained moisture, chafe, fretting, seal displacement, bearing/brake degradation and fastener migration
use coupons or appropriate lab methods if material/coating choices remain ambiguous; do not extrapolate coupon salt-fog time into product life
only after final electrical architecture exists; separately validate insulation, connector, BMS/ESC and fault behavior

cleaning_policy: Do not use a pressure washer unless the final selected components and complete system explicitly support the exposure.
Do not immerse the complete board or traction enclosure merely to discover leaks.
Remove bulk debris with the least aggressive method that preserves seals, bearings, brake surfaces and labels.
Keep solvents/cleaners away from polymers, elastomers, adhesives and coatings unless compatibility is established.
Open protected enclosures only through their intended service procedure; do not make every post-ride inspection require breaking a primary environmental seal.
service_recovery_targets: wheel/tire service remains possible after contamination
mechanical brake releases and actuates normally after cleaning
connectors can be inspected and fully re-seated without using the cable as a handle
no safety-critical fastener or seal must be disturbed merely to remove a replaceable contamination guard
post-ride inspection can identify retained moisture or migration before the next ride
design_principles: Prefer shields, labyrinths, drainage and replaceable contamination barriers over assuming every part is hermetically sealed.
Orient connectors and seams so gravity/drainage help rather than trap water.
Provide drip loops and strain relief before vulnerable cable entries.
Keep brake friction surfaces out of lubricant/cleaner runoff paths.
Treat bearings and moving seals as maintainable wear interfaces rather than lifetime waterproof parts.
Do not make the battery shell the trail skid or contamination sacrificial surface.
A passing inert environmental trial is a packaging/service authority only, not an electrical wet-operation authority.
